Joseph Smith had been recognized as a guardian in another estate, which added complexity to the settlement of his own estate. (Gordon A. Madsen, “Joseph Smith as Guardian: The Lawrence Estate Case,”Journal of Mormon History,vol. 36, no. 3 [Summer 2010], 172–211.)

For a detailed analysis of this case, see Dallin H. Oaks and Joseph I. Bentley, “Joseph Smith and Legal Process: In the Wake of the SteamboatNauvoo,”Brigham Young University Studies,vol. 19, no. 2 (Winter 1979), 192–99.
